messages:
anna: Heads-up — customer ACME-PRV reported sustained 429s and long queue times on their Private VPC tonight. They were at their committed GPUs + ~15% burst for ~20m and we started overflowing request queues. Any canonical guidance we should give them for client-side throttling/backpressure?

mike: Seen this pattern before. Short answer: recommend concurrency caps + token-bucket rate limiting + exponential backoff with jitter. Also add a soft circuit-breaker when 429 rate crosses threshold.

jess: Agree. Also worth surfacing per-tenant queue-length and batch-fill metrics to customers so they can adapt. We should provide concrete config examples they can paste into SDKs.

kevin: Notes from tonight's incident: GPU util was 95% for the worst cluster, avg latency rose from 80ms -> 650ms tail, queue depth metric (inflight_requests) hit 480. Most 429s were immediate (reject) not timeouts.

anna: Can we draft a short recommended client config and guidance bullets? ACME asked for something they can push to their infra team. Keep it conservative (workload: chat + streaming).

mike: Draft configs I use: concurrency_limit=8 per host connection, rate_limit=40 req/s per tenant, token_bucket refill=40/s capacity=80 tokens. Retries: max_retries=4 with backoff base=200ms, jitter=0..300ms. On 429: respect Retry-After if present; else treat as capacity signal and start ramp-down.

jess: Add max_pending_queue=100 to avoid head-of-line blocking and a priority for short inference vs long context. If pending > max_pending_queue, return 503 early (client can implement).

kevin: Practical pseudocode to include for SDKs:
```
# simple client-side admission control pseudocode
if inflight_requests >= concurrency_limit:
    queue.push(request)
elif queue.length > max_pending_queue:
    return error("client_throttled")
else:
    token = token_bucket.take()
    if not token:
        schedule_retry_with_jitter()
    else:
        send(request)
```

jess: Also add a circuit-breaker rule: if 429_rate > 5% over 1m OR error_rate > 2% over 1m, trip to OPEN for 15s then half-open. That prevents cascading retries during cluster saturation.

anna: Good. Any advice on how to size these numbers for Private deployments with varying committed GPUs? Customers want a formula.

mike: Simple heuristic: assume each GPU can sustain ~200 req/s for short generative calls (depends on model/seq). So tenant_rate_limit = floor(committed_gpus * 200 * headroom_factor). Headroom_factor=0.7 for steady state. Example: 4 GPUs -> 4*200*0.7 = 560 req/s. Then apply per-connection concurrency caps and global per-tenant token-bucket.

je ss: (typo) jess: Also account for batch size variance — if customers use bigger batches, per-GPU throughput can increase; recommend they report avg batch sizes so we can suggest per-GPU numbers.

kevin: Networking note: when VPC egress latency spikes (we saw 60ms extra RTT in one AZ), effective per-GPU throughput drops. Recommend customers measure round-trip and include it in capacity calc.

anna: Should we add recommended server-side behavior (what Redwood Private should enforce) — e.g., per-tenant admission limits and graceful 429 payloads with suggested Retry-After and current_queue_depth?

mike: Yes — from infra side we should emit 429 JSON like: `{ "error": "capacity_exceeded", "retry_after": 5, "queue_depth": 120, "suggested_client_rate": 300 }`. That helps client implement adaptive backoff.

jess: We should publish a short KB for customers with: 1) sizing formula, 2) client SDK snippets, 3) recommended retry/backoff/circuit-breaker defaults, 4) observability signals to surface.

oncall-bot: incident #2026-03-18-PRV-AZ2 - auto-alert: high queue_depth observed for tenant ACME-PRV between 01:14 - 01:40 UTC. Pager duty notified.

anna: I'll author the KB draft and include the code snippets. Quick checklist for the doc: sizing example table, client config JSON, SDK pseudocode, server 429 payload spec, metrics to monitor (gpu_util, inflight_requests, queue_depth, 429_rate, avg_batch_size). Anyone want to add final items?

mike: Add guidance on multi-region failover: prefer routing to warm region if latency budget allows; otherwise degrade gracefully.

jess: Add a short tested recipe for streaming workloads: limit simultaneous streams per connection and prefer smaller chunks to avoid long-held GPU slots.

kevin: Also call out billing/cost implications: lowering client concurrency reduces tail latency but increases per-token cost if it forces single-token dispatch. Recommend tenant run small A/B to find sweet spot.

anna: Thanks all — I'll post the KB draft in #docs-review and tag platform for review. :thumbsup:
